**Ch 002 draft — checking for structural damage**

The draft replaces named minor characters (McKee, Catherine) with descriptors ("the photographer," "his wife," "the sister") — this is authorized and clean.

One passage needs attention:

> "His voice faded off and Tom glanced impatiently around the garage."

In the source, Wilson says "I don't mean that… I just meant—" and *then* his voice fades off. In the draft, Tom has just said "No, he doesn't" (coldly), and then "His voice faded off" — but "his" has no clear antecedent: Tom just spoke; Wilson hasn't spoken since "Works pretty slow, don't he?" The "voice fading off" belongs to Wilson in the source, but in the draft the pronoun's antecedent is ambiguous/wrong. A reader would attribute the fading voice to Tom, who just spoke coldly — which is the opposite of what happened. This is a genuine dangling pronoun.

No other structural breaks in Ch 002.

**Ch 003 draft — checking for structural damage**

**"Lucille" passage:**

> "I don't think it's so much that," argued Lucille; "it's more that he was a German spy during the war."

In the source, "Lucille" is introduced two exchanges earlier: *"It was for Lucille, too."* and *"I like to come," Lucille said.* In the draft, those lines are cut. The draft has the girl's companion referenced only as "her companion" (also cut) and the name "Lucille" never appears before this sentence. The draft goes: girl answers Jordan → girl turns to companion → (cut) → another girl says gown-story → Jordan asks → girl confirms → other girl comments → Nick asks → "Gatsby" → leaning together → "killed a man" → Mr. Mumbles listen → **"Lucille"** appears with no prior introduction in the draft.

This is an unglossed minor proper name: Lucille is on the authorized removal list as "Lucille" (authorized minor-character removal). Per the named-person continuity invariant: *"if a proper name from the authorized minor-character list appears in the draft, either the preceding draft chapter or the local sentence/paragraph must identify that person."* The name survives but its introduction was cut; the local sentence gives no identifier.

**"mid-scene jump" / "broken pivot" check for the end of Ch 003:**

> "As I walked down the steps I saw that the evening was not quite over; but I turned away and cut across the lawn toward home."

In the source, what Nick sees is the car-in-the-ditch scene (Owl Eyes). That subplot is authorized to be cut. The draft's "but I turned away" is a pivot contrasting something (the not-quite-over evening) that the draft never shows — but this is a *direct residue of an authorized cut*, so not a finding.

No other structural breaks in Ch 003.
